_: THE CLOCK ORACLE. Twenty-one bars and every column `app/src/components/chart/indicators.js::computeClock` produces for them, RECORDED FROM THAT LANE and asserted by the other one (`tests/test_ast_clock_parity.py`). It is the `self_lag_parity.json` idiom: a lane that drifts fails against the OTHER LANE'S OWN OUTPUT rather than against numbers somebody retyped in a docstring. ⚠️ THIS NOTE ONCE SAID "the thirteen columns" and the count went stale the day six more landed — the exact defect this repo keeps paying for. It names no count now; read `expected`.
_bars: SYNTHETIC AND DELIBERATELY NOT A TRADING SERIES. Three properties are what it is for, and none of them survives in ordinary tape. (1) THE DST FALLBACK: bars 8-12 straddle 2025-11-02, when ET goes 01:59:59 EDT -> 01:00:00 EST, so 01:30 ET occurs TWICE, one UTC hour apart. Both must read hour 1 minute 30; an implementation holding one offset captured at import reads the second as 2:30, and is correct for half the year. (2) A WEEKEND: real US equity bars never print on a Saturday or a Sunday, so `dayofweek` could not cover 7 or 1 from any honest series -- these two days are invented on purpose and the fixture says so rather than implying the tape has them. (3) TWO MIDNIGHTS: bar 5 is 20:00 ET on 2025-10-31, which is 00:00 UTC on the 1st (the trap `VWAP_SESSION_ANCHOR` retired -- it must stay inside the Friday ET day, `sessionfirst` 0), and bar 18 is 00:00 ET, which IS the ET session boundary and must be `sessionfirst` 1.
_barstate_cases: The six barstate columns under each value of `newest_bar_is_forming`. ⚠️ The `null` case has NO equivalent in any pre-2026-09-09 fixture — the retired seam could not express it — so it is new data rather than a re-recording, and it is covered from the other side by `tests/test_bar_close_state.py` and the null-blanks render test in `app/src/components/chart/engine/ast/barstate.test.js`.
_close_cases: ⭐⭐ `time_close`, `time_close("D")` AND `timeframe.change` (C8, 2026-09-28). Each `close_cases` entry is a series and the timeframe it is read under; `close_expected` is what both lanes compute for it. The rules were measured on AMEX:SPY at full history (`tests/fixtures/vendor/harness/vw-clock-close-tfchange-spy-*`) and are stated in `indicators.js::CLOCK_TIME_DERIVED`: the session close as TradingView's calendar applies it (13:00 on a half-day it honours, the week's LAST session on a holiday week, read from the one calendar since 2026-09-28; the `*_half_days` and `weekly_holiday_weeks` cases pin it), and the one 60m bar — 09:30 — whose close depends on which grid the series is on.
_expected: `null` IS NaN, never a value. Every column is aligned to `bars` and exactly as long. Recorded with `tf` = "5", which is why the four timeframe booleans read 1/0/0/0 here; `tf_booleans` is what covers the rest. ⛔ `sessionfirst[0]` IS null AND THAT IS THE COLUMN'S WARM-UP, NOT A GAP IN THE FIXTURE. It reads the PREVIOUS bar's ET day, declares `lookback: 1` for it, and the oldest bar has no previous day to differ from. It read 1 until 2026-08-26; that 1 was a value the WINDOW produced rather than the tape -- slicing this same series at bar 1 or bar 4 made its new leading bar claim to open a session too. The `sliced` block below is what holds that fixed. ⭐⭐ THE SIX BARSTATE COLUMNS WERE ADDED 2026-09-09 and are RECORDED WITH newestBarIsForming=false — the default, which is the screener's true state (every delivered bar is closed at scan time) and NOT a guess. A forming-bar fixture is a separate recording; this one pins the closed-series contract both lanes must agree on.
_iso_daily: ⭐⭐ A DAILY SERIES KEYED BY ISO DATES (Q-T1, 2026-09-28) — the shape the chart's `/api/bars` serves. Under tf "D" each date reads as its session's opening instant, 09:30 America/New_York (`indicators.js::barOpenInstant` / `indicator_compute.bar_open_instant`), which is the instant TradingView stamps as a daily bar's `time`; the series crosses both DST changes, so a fixed UTC offset would miss half of it. Under tf "W" (`iso_weekly_expected`) the same dates stay blank: which day a weekly bar is keyed by is unmeasured, so it is not guessed.
_newest_bar_is_forming: ⭐⭐ THE TRI-STATE, AND IT REPLACED A `now`. `true` / `false` / `null`, handed in per fetch and produced upstream by `indicator_compute.bar_close_state` — the only place the NYSE closure and early-close sets are read. ⛔ `null` MEANS UNKNOWN AND NEVER MEANS FALSE: under it the four CLOCK_REALTIME columns are blank, while the extent pair (`islast`, `isfirst`) still answers because it reads only the fetch's shape. `barstate_cases` pins all three so a future edit cannot collapse unknown onto false and stay green.
_non_instant: THE UNIT GATE, AND IT IS PARTIAL. `non_instant_bars` is the same series with `t` rewritten as `bars_sqlite`'s YYYYMMDD ints -- exactly what the alert and scan lanes hand a daily series, and what once made `compute_vwap` anchor 400 daily bars in 1970. The eight time-derived columns must ALL be null; `barindex` and the four timeframe booleans must be UNTOUCHED, because they read no `t` and a guard firing on them would refuse a column it has no reason to doubt. ⭐ THE BARSTATE SIX SURVIVE THE UNIT GATE, deliberately: they read no t at all, so a YYYYMMDD series still gets them — the same reason barindex does. Their values here are IDENTICAL to the instant series above, which is the assertion.
_recorder: ⛔ GENERATED — DO NOT HAND-EDIT. Rewrite with `python tools/record_clock_parity.py`; check with `--check`. Inputs (`bars`, `non_instant_bars`, `iso_daily_bars`, `close_cases`, `tf`, and the `tf_booleans` / `sliced_sessionfirst` key sets) are READ from this file and written back unchanged — only the expected blocks are recomputed, so the series the numbers describe stays nameable. Canonical by construction: sorted keys, two-space indent, LF, and integral floats emitted as ints.
_sliced_sessionfirst: ⭐ WINDOW-INDEPENDENCE, FROZEN. Each key is a bar index; its value is what `sessionfirst` must be for `bars[k:]` -- and it is the FULL series' own answer from bar k on, with the first element blanked because that bar is now the warm-up bar. ⛔ THE POINT IS THE TAIL: from the second bar of any slice, the answer must be IDENTICAL to the full series. Before the warm-up pad it was not -- `bars[1:]` read [1,0,1,0] where the full series read [0,0,1,0] -- so a chart scrolled one bar to the left drew a session marker on a bar that opens nothing.
_tf_booleans: THE TIMEFRAME VOCABULARY, PINNED ACROSS THE LANES. Each key is the `tf` handed to `computeClock`; `__absent__` is no argument at all. The four values are that timeframe's flat answer. THE `null` ROWS ARE THE POINT: `3`, `1H`, `2D`, `d` and the empty string are not codes this platform ships, and an unrecognised code answers NOT-COMPUTABLE rather than a confident 0 -- the same answer an absent `tf` gets. A lane that guessed from the string's SHAPE would call `3` intraday and `2D` daily, and this block goes red for both. The eight real codes are the one list each lane spells for itself, so this is where a divergence between the two surfaces.
